title: Scottish Labour councillor failed to declare role in ‘gender critical’ group, breaching Council rules amid trade union legal action
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Scottish Labour councillor failed to declare role in ‘gender critical’ group, breaching Council rules amid trade union legal action

A ‘gender critical’ Scottish Labour executive committee member and councillor failed to declare on her register of interests the company she set up to sue her trade union, in an apparent breach of the Scottish Councillors’ Code of Conduct

Actual Article Body:
A Scottish Labour councillor will be in court next Friday (25 September) to attempt to force her trade union to implement the EHRC’s “trans-exclusionary” guidance. But, in an apparent breach of her legal obligations as a councillor, she has not declared her role in the private company she set up to fight the legal case - QueerAF

Since October 2025, councillor Alison Ann-Dowling has been on the board of directors of ‘gender critical’ company Adult Female Trade Unionists – yet this role does not appear on her councillor’s register of interests, QueerAF can reveal.

Ann-Dowling has been the councillor for Renfrewshire ward 10, which comprises the small villages of Houston, Crosslee, and Linwood in the west of Scotland, since 2017. A member of the Community union, which represents workers regardless of the sector they work in, she is also the deputy leader of the Labour Group on Renfrewshire Council and sits on Scottish Labour’s executive committee.

Adult Female Trade Unionists, or ADFEMTUS LTD, is a private company that Ann-Dowling and former Edinburgh councillor Norma Austin Hart set up to campaign for “women’s sex-based rights in the trade union movement”. Its purpose is listed as “trade union activities” - Companies House

However, despite Ann-Dowling’s legal obligations to report such interests, this appointment does not currently appear on her register of interests as a councillor for Renfrewshire Council.

Eleven months ago, at the gender-critical FiLiA 2025 conference, Ann-Dowling and Hart publicly declared that they would be launching a crowdfunding campaign for the legal costs of the upcoming case. But in a statement to QueerAF, Ann-Dowling said that they in fact did “not establish a crowdfunder” and that the legal costs of the case would be “met by a private donor”.

“I am an unpaid Director of an organisation established to campaign for women’s rights,” Ann-Dowling told QueerAF. “I am in the process of noting it [in] my register of interests.”

Ann-Dowling and Hart announced plans to sue their union, Community, over its Equality Policy in a Substack publication called The Frontline. Community’s policy refers to “women and non-binary people” in its gender section, which Ann-Dowling and Hart claim goes against the April 2025 Supreme Court ruling on the Equality Act - Personnel Today

The women are also making claims of victimisation, as they claim they were threatened with disciplinary action following the initial Substack post.

A Community spokesperson told QueerAF they are “an inclusive trade union committed to increasing gender diversity” within its democratic and leadership structures.

“Our Gender Equality Strategy reaffirms that commitment and supports the steps we are taking to build a more representative union. We strongly refute suggestions that the union has acted unlawfully, and remain confident that our approach is consistent with both our values and our obligations.”

In April 2026, Ann-Dowling and Hart were granted permission to proceed with their judicial review of the policy in Scotland’s Court of Session, which handles high-level civil cases. Their hearing is due to take place on September 25 in Edinburgh, as listed on the Scottish Courts and Tribunals website - The Scotsman

The women are represented by Balfour + Manson LLP, the same firm that represented For Women Scotland in their successful bid to exclude trans people from being recognised as the correct gender under the Equality Act 2010 - Supreme Court

The Scottish Councillors’ Code of Conduct states in section 4.22 that councillors must register non-financial interests, defined as “those which members of the public with knowledge of the relevant facts might reasonably think could influence my actions, speeches, votes or decision-making in my council”.

They must register these interests within a month of any changes occurring. Relevant interests include being a member or holding an office in public bodies, companies, and trade unions.
